LESSON: MYSELF ENVIRONMENT

Grade: PP1
Subject: ENVIRONMENTAL ACTIVITIES
Strand: SOCIAL
Topic 1.1: Myself ENVIRONMENT

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello learner! Today we will learn about Myself ENVIRONMENT. Read carefully, study the examples, do the practice, then try the revision quiz.

Big question: What is your name?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. tell their names for identity
2. identify their sex for self-awareness
3. identify body parts (head, hands and legs)
4. appreciate oneself for self-esteem hands and legs) picture reading on body parts from charts parts about themselves.

SECTION 3: LEARN STEP BY STEP

1. tell their names for identity
   In this part of the lesson, you learn to tell their names for identity. Think about how you can do this at school and at home in Kenya.

2. identify their sex for self-awareness
   In this part of the lesson, you learn to identify their sex for self-awareness. Think about how you can do this at school and at home in Kenya.

3. identify body parts (head, hands and legs)

SECTION 4: EXAMPLES

Example 1: At school, pick litter and put it in the bin. That cares for the environment.

Example 2: Wash your hands with soap before eating and after using the toilet.

Example 3: Name two foods you eat at home that help you grow strong.

SECTION 5: TRY THIS

1. Read the examples above again. Underline two new words or ideas about Myself ENVIRONMENT.
2. Explain Myself ENVIRONMENT to a parent or classmate using your own words and one Kenyan example.
3. Try this activity: You should tell 1. What is your name? ENVIRONMENT strand the learner should be their names 2. Are you a boy or a girl? (5 Lessons) able to;
4. Show that you can: tell their names for identity
5. Complete the Work to do section, then attempt the Revision Quiz. Check Answers only after you finish.

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (PRACTICE & REVISION)

1. Write five sentences about Myself ENVIRONMENT. Use examples from your school, home, or market.
2. Answer this question in your exercise book: What is your name?
3. Make a short oral presentation (about one minute) to your parent or teacher.
4. List three ways you will practise this topic this week.
